property_summary: After initialize is called with any parameters, c.baseToken() must equal the _baseToken argument passed in; the buggy version leaves baseToken as address(0), so the rule is violated whenever a non-zero _baseToken is supplied.

After a successful initialize (with feeRate <= 5000 so it does not legitimately revert), c.baseToken() must equal the _baseToken argument; the mutant drops the assignment so baseToken stays address(0) for any non-zero _baseToken.

After initialize completes, c.changeFee() must equal the _changeFee argument passed in, for any admissible input; the mutant stores _feeRate into changeFee, so any input with _changeFee != _feeRate violates this rule.

After a pool is initialized, any subsequent initialize call must revert with AlreadyInitialized and leave ALL parameters, in particular changeFee, unchanged; the buggy version writes changeFee before the initialized check, so a second initialize call silently overwrites changeFee even though the call reverts.

initialize is one-shot: once initialized, any second initialize call reverts and must leave changeFee unchanged (equal to the value set by the first call), but the buggy version writes changeFee before the initialized check, so a reverted second call silently overwrites changeFee.
